דַּעְתּוֹ וּרְצוֹנוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ שֶׁאֵינֶנּוּ חָפֵץ בֶּאֱמֶת כָּזֶה שֶׁל קִטְרוּגִים וּמַחֲלֹקֶת, מִמֵּילָא נִתְבַּטֵל קִטְרוּג הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁכָּל הָעוֹלָם מָלֵא קְטָטוֹת. כִּי עַל־יְדֵי הַדֶּרֶךְ הַזֶּה שֶׁתֵּכֶף כְּשֶׁרוֹאִין שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר לָבוֹא לִידֵי מַחֲלֹקֶת עַל־יְדֵי רִבּוּי הָאֱמֶת, אֲזַי מְצֻוֶּה לְסַלֵּק הָאֱמֶת קְצָת וּלְהַשְׁלִיכוֹ מֵעַל פָּנָיו, וְלֹא יִסְתַּכֵּל עַל הָרָע שֶׁבַּחֲבֵרוֹ כְּלָל רַק עַל הַטּוֹב שֶׁבּוֹ וְיָדִין אוֹתוֹ לְכַף זְכוּת עַל־יְדֵי זֶה מִמֵּילָא נַעֲשָׂה שָׁלוֹם בָּעוֹלָם. וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זַ"ל מֻתָּר לְשַׁנּוֹת בִּדְבַר הַשָּׁלוֹם, כִּי זֶה עֶצֶם הָאֱמֶת שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ חָפֵץ בּוֹ, לְשַׁנּוֹת קְצָת הָאֱמֶת בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁצְּרִיכִין לָזֶה מִפְּנֵי הַשָּׁלוֹם, וְדַיְקָא עַל־יְדֵי זֶה זוֹכֶה לְהַכְנִיס בָּעוֹלָם נְקֻדַּת הָאֱמֶת לַאֲמִתּוֹ כַּמְּבֹאָר בִּפְנִים. וְזֶה בְּחִינַת הָאֱמֶת וְהַשָּׁלוֹם אֱהָבוּ (הל' רבית ה"ה אות לד לה). כא. עִקַּר עֲבוֹדַת ה' הוּא בְּחִינַת שָׁלוֹם, וּבִשְׁבִיל זֶה הָיָה עִקַּר בְּרִיאַת הָאָדָם. כִּי הָאָדָם כָּלוּל מֵחֹמֶר וְצוּרָה, גּוּף מִן הַתַּחְתּוֹנִים וּנְשָׁמָה מִן הָעֶלְיוֹנִים, וְהֵם שְׁנֵי הֲפָכִים מַמָּשׁ. וּכְשֶׁהוֹלֵךְ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם אַחַר שְׁרִירוּת לִבּוֹ וְתַאֲווֹת גּוּפוֹ הָרָעִים, אֲזַי הוּא הֶעְדֵּר הַשָּׁלוֹם כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר, אֵין שָׁלוֹם בַּעֲצָמַי מִפְּנֵי חַטָּאתִי. אֲבָל כְּשֶׁכּוֹפֶה אֶת גּוּפוֹ וּמְבַטְּלוֹ לִרְצוֹן הַנְּשָׁמָה זֶהוּ בְּחִינַת שָׁלוֹם, שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה שָׁלוֹם בֵּין הַנְּשָׁמָה וְהַגּוּף. וְעַל־יְדֵי עֲבוֹדָתוֹ הוּא מְקַשֵּׁר כָּל הָעוֹלָמוֹת יַחַד לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, דָּרֵי מַעְלָה עִם דָּרֵי מַטָּה, וְעוֹשֶׂה שָׁלוֹם בֵּין כֻּלָּם בֵּין כָּל הַהֲפָכִים, כִּי מְקַשֵּׁר כֻּלָּם לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, שֶׁזֶּה בְּחִינַת שָׁלוֹם. כִּי בִּשְׁבִיל זֶה נִבְרָא הָאָדָם בְּשִׁשִּׁי מִן הָעֶלְיוֹנִים וְהַתַּחְתּוֹנִים כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה קִנְאָה בְּמַעֲשֵׂה בְּרֵאשִׁית כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זַ"ל שֶׁזֶּה בְּחִינַת שָׁלוֹם.
aligned_segments.en:
The Torah is called peace — as it is written: "all her paths are peace" . And the essential fullness of peace is when it is in the aspect of peace that has a mouth — in the aspect of: "let me speak of peace in you" . And therefore one must read the Torah — which is the aspect of peace — specifically with one's mouth — so that it be in the aspect of peace that has a mouth — the essential fullness of peace. And then specifically one merits life — in the aspect of: "for they are life to those who find them" — and our Rabbis expounded: "to those who bring them forth with their mouth" — for the essential life is received specifically through peace. And this is also the aspect of: "length of days and years of life and peace" . For the essential life is through the connection of the soul with the body — two opposites — and through peace they connect together and one merits life. And the remedy too is through peace — in the aspect of: "peace, peace to the far and to the near, says Hashem, and I will heal them" . And since the essential peace one merits through Torah is through faith in the Sages — and faith in the Sages flows from the aspect of a vow [neder] — the aspect of Binah — the aspect of the supernal pleasantness — as brought — and this is the aspect of: "its ways are ways of pleasantness — and all its paths are peace."

Translator's Summary — Shalom V'Achdus (Peace, Unity, Love of Friends) The longest chapter since Tzadik, at 68 entries. The chapter's thesis is that peace is not merely a social virtue — it is the cosmic mechanism through which separated fragments of the divine light can be received without shattering. Every soul of Israel is a vessel — and the light of G-dliness requires all vessels assembled together in love and peace to be received safely. This is why the Torah required 600,000 present at Sinai, and why love of one's neighbor is declared the great principle of the Torah.

A recurring and powerful idea is the interplay between truth and peace (entry 20): Hashem cast truth to the ground not because truth is unimportant, but because a truth that fuels accusation and dispute is not the truth He desires. The Torah-scholar knows to set aside divisive truth for peace's sake — and paradoxically, this specific yielding is itself the truest path to bringing genuine truth into the world.

Entry 52 distinguishes partial peace from general peace: not harming one's fellow is partial; giving of one's own to another, yielding beyond obligation — that is the general peace. And the same principle applies inward: not sinning is partial inner peace; fully subordinating all bodily desires to the soul is the complete inner peace.

The chapter culminates (entry 65) in the vision of Mashiach: the Second Temple was destroyed through baseless hatred — and the rebuilt Temple will stand on the foundation of love and totality. Eliyahu's mission is to make peace — and through peace the halachah will be clarified and the redemption will come.

— This summary is from the translator. All content above is a faithful rendering of the original Hebrew source text of Otzar HaYirah, Volume IV. Na Nach Nachma Nachman MayUman.
